title: Grade 7 Math — Mon, Jun 09
description: Simple & Compound Interest — Day 1 of 5: Review SI; introducing CI
subject: mathematics

questions.question: In SI, interest earned each year is ___.
questions.explanation: In simple interest the same fixed amount of interest is added each year.

questions.question: In Compound Interest (CI), interest is calculated on ___.
options: The future value minus the principal
questions.explanation: CI is calculated on the principal PLUS all the interest earned so far. This is 'interest on interest'.

questions.question: If P = ₹1000 at 10% per year for 2 years (SI), how much interest is earned?
For P = ₹1000 at 10% per year (CI, annually), interest in Year 1 = ___.
After Year 1 of CI (P=₹1000, R=10%), the new principal for Year 2 is ___.
questions.explanation: Amount after Year 1 = 1000 + 100 = ₹1100. This becomes the principal for Year 2.

questions.question: For CI Year 2 (new principal ₹1100, R=10%), interest = ___.
questions.explanation: 10% of ₹1100 = ₹110. One key difference from SI (which would be ₹100).

questions.question: After 2 years, CI on ₹1000 at 10% = ___.
questions.explanation: Year 1 interest: ₹100. Year 2 interest: ₹110. Total CI = ₹210.

questions.question: For same P, R, T — which is MORE: SI or CI?
questions.explanation: CI is always greater than SI for T > 1 year because CI includes 'interest on interest'.

questions.question: CI − SI for same P, R, T is called ___.
options: Both A and B are used
questions.explanation: The difference (CI − SI) shows how much more compound interest earns over simple interest.

questions.question: P = ₹2000 at 5% per year for 1 year. Is CI equal to SI?
questions.explanation: For exactly 1 year, CI = SI because there is no 'previous interest' to compound on.

questions.question: Amount (A) = ___.
questions.explanation: Amount = Principal + Interest (whether simple or compound).

questions.question: P = ₹10000 at 6% per year. After 2 years SI = ___.
Which type of interest grows faster over many years?
options: Both grow at the same rate
questions.explanation: Compound interest grows exponentially (faster and faster) while SI grows linearly (same amount each year).
